title: Household expense difficulty tracks loneliness and support gaps more than contact frequency
source_unit: US Census Bureau March 2026 HTOPS/HPS public-use person respondent, conditioned on household expense difficulty

denominator.unit: respondents with valid EXPENSE_DIFFICULT code; PUF total rows 12521

observations.method: Corrected March 2026 HTOPS/HPS PUF; respondent PWEIGHT for point estimates and PWEIGHT1–PWEIGHT80 successive-difference replicate weights for standard errors. Outcome-specific valid codes and denominators apply.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive cross-sectional conditional shares. Expense is household-reported, social outcomes are respondent-reported, clocks differ by item, and no causal or longitudinal interpretation is implied.
observations.subgroup: All valid expense-difficulty groups; social outcomes are frequent loneliness (SOC_LONELY 1/2), low social/emotional support (SOC_SUPPORT 4/5), frequent contact (SOC_TALK 4), and food insufficiency (FD_SUFF 3/4).
observations.counterinterpretation: Contact frequency can persist while perceived support worsens; some respondents without expense difficulty still report loneliness or low support; a common unmeasured health, work, housing, or relationship condition may shape both sides.

observations.period: March 13–30, 2026; endpoint expense groups conditioned on respondent age

denominator.unit: respondents in age-band × endpoint expense cells; age bands 25–44, 45–64, and 65+

observations.method: Same corrected March 2026 PUF and 80 replicate weights; age bands are TAGE 25–44, 45–64, and 65+, with endpoint EXPENSE_DIFFICULT codes 1 and 4.
observations.uncertainty: Subgroup-conditioned descriptive shares; endpoint cells are smaller and have wider standard errors. No age interaction or causal moderation test is claimed.
observations.subgroup: Respondent age bands and no-difficulty versus very-difficult household expense groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Persistence within age bands does not identify an expense effect; the different loneliness and support patterns may reflect health, work, household, or relationship composition.

related_sources.claim: Corrected March 2026 HTOPS/HPS PUF, replicate-weight file, and data dictionary archive.

boundary: This record documents a same-round descriptive bridge from household expense difficulty to respondent social-connection and food-sufficiency measures. It does not establish a dated bill, actor, practical help, remedy, recovery, trust change, community engagement, political action, or longitudinal causal pathway.
